descriptionChirho: Feminine noun עֻגָה denoting a round, flat cake or bread-cake baked on coals or hot stones, used in narratives of miraculous provision (1 Kgs 17:13, 19:6) and ritual contexts (Gen 18:6; Exod 12:39; Num 11:8; Ezek 4:12). All three clusters represent the same baked-food concept across number and syntactic variation: plural 'cakes' (S122350), singular/construct 'cake / cake of' (S122352), and conjunction-prefixed 'and cake of' (S122351). Multilingual evidence confirms a unified sense: Spanish 'torta(s),' Hindi 'रोटी / रोटियां,' Arabic 'أَقْرَاص / كَعْكَة,' Korean '떡 / 빵 / 과자,' Swahili 'mkate / mikate.' The singular-plural distinction is grammatical, not semantic.
